event: During a flight of VXE 942 with OGCS 1.3.3, OGCS showed Reconnecting after 21 minutes and the VSM entered lost link logic, though telemetry and commands kept working; the aircraft landed normally.
failure_mode: auth token refresh opened a second WebSocket instead of reusing the first; when one closed, OGCS reported a full disconnect, showed Reconnecting and stopped sending heartbeats to the VSM
contributing: poor C2 and RF conditions in flight
operator did not refresh the page in flight, as the OGCS dialog warns

evidence.quote: From the VSM’s info log, the 1 Hz periodic heartbeat stopped entirely at 14:51:02 (22:51:02 UTC) and never resumed.
Analysis of the code indicates the auth refresh logic is flawed, causing two WebSocket connections to be opened rather than reusing the existing connection.
When one of the two connections closes, the system incorrectly reports a full disconnection despite the other remaining open and receiving telemetry.
The first was due to an auth token expiring, which was successfully refreshed and reconnected after ~5 seconds.

team_root_cause: Logic error in OGCS causing it to show ‘Reconnecting…’ and not send Heartbeats to the VSM despite having a good connection.
reasoning: VSM logs show the OGCS heartbeat stopped at 14:51:02 and never returned, while waypoint and go-to commands still arrived. OGCS logs show an abnormal WebSocket disconnect at exactly that time, after an auth token refresh, and code review found the refresh opened a duplicate WebSocket whose closing was read as a full disconnect. The fix shipped in OGCS 1.4.0.
notes: The v12.8 fault in the XCOMM logs is the heated pitot tripping the 3 A 12 V limit, noted as unrelated. OGCS-526 was later closed as overtaken by a STANAG 4586 refactor of the Reconnecting logic.
